goals: Validation: reproduce the daily streamflow hydrograph at the American River nr Nile gauge and report NSE
Mechanistic (supporting): characterize elevation- and soil-controlled runoff generation (snowmelt timing, surface runoff vs sub-surface drainage) across the contributing basin
key_processes: water partitioning: surface runoff vs sub-surface drainage vs ET
baseflow / drainage timing (requires equilibrated water table)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves per-location snow, ET and runoff generation, but produces no integrated/routed streamflow; a gauge hydrograph is therefore only reachable via an unbuilt aggregation+routing step.

answerable: per-column runoff generation (QOVER, QDRAI, QRUNOFF) across elevation/soil strata
snowpack accumulation and melt timing (H2OSNO, SNOW, QSNOMELT) driven by NLDAS orographic precip/temperature

not_answerable.aspect: Daily streamflow hydrograph at the gauge and its NSE
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral transport and no runoff routing: per-column QRUNOFF cannot be aggregated to the contributing area and routed to the gauge with correct timing/baseflow — there is no native integrated streamflow.
not_answerable.needs: runoff aggregation + streamflow routing to gauge

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation band x dominant soil), placed within the American River contributing area

classes: dominant SSURGO texture per band (native, resolved downstream)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Three elevation bands span the precip-phase/snow gradient that shapes the hydrograph; sampling the dominant soil in each band (~3 columns/band) captures partitioning without a blind grid. 9 columns is the smallest set that resolves the runoff-generation heterogeneity feeding any future aggregation.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate at the rain-snow transition (800-1400 m) where melt-timing controls freshet shape; anchor one band in the snow zone (headwater generation) and one in the valley (rain response, riparian drainage).
sampling_strategy.replication: Light: multiple columns per band spanning aspect/soil variation to average sub-12km terrain the forcing cannot resolve.

sampling_plan.reason: Captures low-elevation rain-driven runoff and riparian sub-surface drainage that sustains baseflow at the gauge.
Isolates the melt-timing zone that dominates the spring freshet shape of the hydrograph — the most sensitive control on any NSE.
Captures snowpack accumulation and late-melt runoff generation from the upper contributing area.

validation_design.observation_source: USGS gauge: American River nr Nile (daily)
validation_design.comparison: aggregated — area-weighted sum of per-column QRUNOFF over the contributing area, then routed to the gauge; NSE only computable AFTER routing exists. Absent routing, only a partial comparison of aggregated runoff volume/seasonality is possible (NOT a daily NSE).
validation_design.metric: NSE (daily) — blocked; interim: monthly/seasonal runoff volume bias and correlation

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (elevation-resolved), native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + spin-up years for equilibrated drainage/baseflow

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff aggregation + streamflow routing to gauge
requires_capabilities.why: Convert independent per-column QRUNOFF into an integrated, time-routed hydrograph at the American River gauge.
requires_capabilities.blocks: The entire request: daily hydrograph reproduction and NSE.

requires_capabilities.capability: contributing-area / drainage-basin delineation for the gauge
requires_capabilities.why: Define which columns and areas contribute to the gauge and their area weights.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Aggregation weighting; correct total runoff volume.

requires_capabilities.capability: multi-year spin-up / WTD-informed warm start (per column)
requires_capabilities.why: Baseflow and drainage timing require an equilibrated water table; cold-start ZWD/recharge are artifacts.

requires_capabilities.capability: SSURGO gridded soil sampling per column
requires_capabilities.why: Soil texture controls surface-runoff vs drainage partitioning.

assumptions: American River nr Nile drains a sub-area within the Naches bbox; its contributing area must be delineated (not provided).
NLDAS-2 covers this CONUS basin, giving orographically varying precip/temperature across the 352-1977 m relief.
Daily gauge record overlaps the 1980-2018 forcing window.
open_questions: What is the delineated contributing area (and its column weights) for the American River gauge?
Is a routing/aggregation module planned, or should the deliverable be redefined as aggregated runoff volume/seasonality (which the runs CAN produce) rather than daily NSE?
Which years should be the evaluation period, and how many spin-up years are acceptable given NLDAS cost (~30 min/simulated-year/column)?
